answer.what_it_does: Feedzai provides AI-powered fraud and financial crime prevention for banks and fintechs, covering fraud, AML, and related risk workflows in real time.[1][2] It combines models, shared intelligence, rules, and AI agents to help teams detect risk, investigate alerts, and act faster across onboarding, payments, and compliance operations.[2][5]

ai_agents.name: Farol
ai_agents.what_it_does: An always-on AI agent embedded in Feedzai RiskOps Studio that helps fraud and AML teams analyze rules, investigate alerts, and draft suspicious activity reports.[3][6]
actions: Interrogates and analyzes rule sets
Flags rules that generate noise without catching fraud
Retrieves and summarizes alert data
Drafts suspicious activity reports (SARs)
Provides contextual answers inside RiskOps Studio
Works within fraud and AML team workflows

actions: Connects external AI agents to Feedzai data
Uses shared context across agents
Runs alongside Feedzai-native and third-party agents
Integrates with risk workflows and analysis
Supports secure connections to bank workflows

incidents_or_risks.what: Feedzai says fraudsters may use AI agents too, and it is building detection to verify who authorized an agent, what it can do, and whether its behavior still matches intent.[3][4]
The company describes the need to detect agentic attacks, including agent takeovers, agent botnets, and malware, as banking becomes more agentic.[3][4]

facts.claim: Feedzai says it stops fraud and financial crime in real time with AI that catches risk and an AI agent that helps teams act and respond faster.[1]

Its platform is designed to detect fraud across inbound and outbound transactions and multiple payment rails, including card fraud, account takeover, synthetic identity, scams, money mules, phishing, and malware.[2]
Feedzai’s AML solution blends rules and machine learning to detect criminal activity, reduce false positives, prioritize alerts, and integrate SAR submission.[5]
RiskOps unifies identity across channels to detect fraud and money laundering risk from onboarding to remediation.[7]
Feedzai says its transaction fraud tools evaluate payments and transfers in real time using transaction history, customer behavior, and predictive intelligence.[8]
Feedzai says its retail bank offerings combine long-term and real-time data, behavioral biometrics, device signals, and network attributes to identify fraud typologies.[14]
Feedzai says its AML tools support workflows to investigate, manage cases, and report suspicious activity on one platform.[15]

answer.what_it_does: Feedzai provides an AI-native fraud and financial crime prevention platform (RiskOps) that unifies identity and risk signals across the customer lifecycle to detect fraud and money laundering risk in real time. It also includes an embedded AI agent (Farol) to accelerate investigations, rule analysis, and SAR drafting within financial crime/risk workflows.

Agent protection/detection: includes detection to verify who authorized an agent and constrain whether the agent’s actions match intended behavior

facts.claim: Feedzai was founded in 2011 and describes itself as an end-to-end AI-native platform for stopping fraud and financial crime.
Feedzai says its platform is built on Amazon Web Services cloud infrastructure and can ingest third-party and internal data through APIs and adapters.
Feedzai reports that the world's top banks, payment networks and acquirers use its technology to safeguard more than one billion consumers and $9 trillion in payment volume each year.
Feedzai IQ Score, launched June 9, 2026, is a network-derived fraud risk scoring product delivered through a single API that uses federated learning so raw customer data is not shared.
Feedzai reports 4x more fraud detected and 50% fewer alerts for IQ Score versus traditional rules-based approaches; this is a company-reported figure.
RiskFM, announced March 24, 2026, is described by Feedzai as a tabular foundation model for fraud, AML and broader risk decisions, trained on onboarding, digital, payment and AML workflow data.
Feedzai's AML offering uses rules and AI to prioritise alerts so investigators can focus on high-risk cases.
Feedzai's AML page says its AI agents are meant to reduce false positives and focus teams on the riskiest alerts.

Feedzai's platform is described as combining fraud detection and AML workflows into one decisioning layer, which Chartis-type analyst recognition cited in a 2025 SPARK Matrix placement for Financial Crime and Compliance data management.
Feedzai was named a Best-in-Class vendor in an Aite-Novarica Group fraud and AML machine learning platform report, which cited its single risk engine and ease of use.
Feedzai has been named a winner of the AML Mule Detection award in Chartis' Financial Crime and Compliance50 (FCC50) 2026 ranking.

Feedzai and Mastercard announced in February 2025 a partnership to expand Mastercard's Consumer Fraud Risk scam solution to more markets using Feedzai's platform, which Mastercard said was available in over 90 countries.
Feedzai's Fraud Readiness Index 2026 surveyed more than 1,000 senior fraud leaders across 12 countries.
Feedzai has said the European Central Bank concluded a framework agreement with it as the first-ranked tenderer.
